en: Abu Hurayrah said: Abu Jahl said: "Does Muhammad dust his face in the dust in front of you?" It was said: "Yes." He said: "By al-Lat and al-'Uzza, if I see him doing that, I will certainly trample upon his neck, or I will smear his face in the dust!" He said: So he came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, while he was praying, intending to trample upon his neck. He said: Nothing surprised them from him except that he was turning back on his heels and shielding himself with his hands. He said: It was said to him: "What is the matter with you?" He said: "Indeed, between me and him is a trench of fire, terror, and wings." The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "If he had drawn near to me, the angels would have snatched him limb by limb." He said: Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed—we do not know whether it is in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah or something that reached him: {"No! Indeed, man transgresses, because he sees himself self-sufficient. Indeed, to your Lord is the return. Have you seen the one who forbids a servant when he prays? Have you seen if he is upon guidance, or enjoins righteousness? Have you seen if he denies and turns away"}—meaning Abu Jahl—{"Does he not know that Allah sees? No! If he does not desist, We will surely drag him by the forelock—a lying, sinning forelock. Then let him call his associates; We will call the angels of Hell. No! Do not obey him"}. 'Ubaydullah added in his hadith: he said: and He commanded him with what He commanded him with. And Ibn 'Abd al-A'la added: "Then let him call his associates"—meaning his people.

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh al-'Anbari narrated to us: My father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Hamid az-Ziyadi, that he heard Anas ibn Malik say: Abu Jahl said: "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment." So there was revealed: {"And Allah would not punish them while you are among them, nor would Allah punish them while they seek forgiveness. And what have they that Allah should not punish them while they prevent people from al-Masjid al-Haram..."} to the end of the verse.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us; (and a different chain) Ibn Numayr narrated to us: My father narrated to us; (and a different chain) Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Jarir reported to us; (and a different chain) Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, all of them from al-A'mash with this chain of narration, similar to the hadith of Waki', and in the hadith of Jarir he said: "I was a blacksmith in the pre-Islamic days of ignorance, and I did some work for al-'As ibn Wa'il, so I came to him to demand payment."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and 'Abdullah ibn Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us—and the wording is 'Abdullah's—they said: Waki' narrated to us: Al-A'mash narrated to us, from Abu ad-Duha, from Masruq, from Khabbab, who said: I was owed a debt by al-'As ibn Wa'il, so I went to him to demand payment. He said to me: "I will never pay you until you disbelieve in Muhammad." He said: I said to him: "I will never disbelieve in Muhammad until you die and then be resurrected." He said: "Am I truly to be resurrected after death? Then I will pay you when I return to wealth and children." Waki' said: thus al-A'mash said. He said: So this verse was revealed: {"Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our verses and said, 'I will surely be given wealth and children'?"} up to His words: {"and he comes to Us alone"}.

Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, saying: I heard 'Abdullah ibn Idris say: I heard al-A'mash narrating it from 'Abdullah ibn Murrah, from Masruq, from 'Abdullah, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, was in a palm grove leaning on a palm-stalk branch... then he mentioned the like of their hadith from al-A'mash, and said in his narration: "and you have not been given of knowledge except a little."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us; (and a different chain) Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanthali and 'Ali ibn Khashram both narrated to us: 'Isa ibn Yunus reported to us, both from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqamah, from 'Abdullah, who said: I was walking with the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, in a cultivated field in Madinah... similar to the hadith of Hafs, except that in the hadith of Waki': "and you have not been given of knowledge except a little," while in the hadith of 'Isa ibn Yunus: "and they have not been given," from the narration of Ibn Khashram.

'Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us: My father narrated to us: Al-A'mash narrated to us: Ibrahim narrated to me, from 'Alqamah, from 'Abdullah, who said: While I was walking with the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, in a cultivated land while he was leaning on a palm-stalk branch, he passed by a group of Jews. Some of them said to others: "Ask him about the soul." Others said: "What drives you to ask him? Lest he confront you with something you dislike." They said: "Ask him." So one of them stood up to him and asked him about the soul. He said: The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, remained silent and gave him no reply, so I knew that revelation was coming to him. He said: I stood in my place, and when the revelation descended, he said: {"And they ask you about the soul. Say, 'The soul is of the affair of my Lord. And you have not been given of knowledge except a little'"}.

Yahya ibn Habib al-Harithi narrated to us: Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated to us: Qurrah narrated to us: Muhammad narrated to us, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "If ten of the Jews had followed me, no Jew would have remained on the surface of the earth except that he embraced Islam."

'Abd al-Malik ibn Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth narrated to me: My father narrated to me, from my grandfather: Khalid ibn Yazid narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said: "On the Day of Resurrection, the earth will be like a single loaf of bread, which the Compeller will turn in His Hand just as one of you turns his loaf of bread while traveling, as hospitality for the people of Paradise." He said: A man from the Jews came and said: "May the Most Merciful bless you, O Abu al-Qasim! Shall I not inform you of the hospitality of the people of Paradise on the Day of Resurrection?" He said: "Yes." He said: "The earth will be like a single loaf of bread"—just as the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said. He said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, looked at us and then laughed until his premolars showed. The Jew said: "Shall I not inform you of their condiment?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Their condiment will be Balam and Nun." They asked: "What is that?" He said: "An ox and a giant fish, from the extra lobe of whose livers seventy thousand will eat."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: 'Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from Dawud, from ash-Sha'bi, from Masruq, from 'A'ishah, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: {"On the Day the earth will be replaced by another earth, and the heavens as well"}: "Where will the people be on that Day, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Upon the Sirat (Bridge)."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Abi Kathir: Abu Hazim ibn Dinar narrated to me, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Mankind will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection upon a white, reddish-white land like a flat loaf of pure flour, with no landmark for anyone on it."

Surayj ibn Yunus and Harun ibn 'Abdullah both narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Isma'il ibn Umayyah reported to me, from Ayyub ibn Khalid, from 'Abdullah ibn Rafi', the freed slave of Umm Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, took my hand and said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created the soil on Saturday, created the mountains in it on Sunday, created the trees on Monday, created adversity on Tuesday, created light on Wednesday, dispersed beasts in it on Thursday, and created Adam, peace be upon him, after 'Asr on Friday, at the very end of creation, during the last hour of the hours of Friday, between 'Asr and the night." Ibrahim said: Al-Bistami—namely al-Husayn ibn 'Isa—Sahl ibn 'Ammar, Ibrahim ibn Bint Hafs, and others narrated this hadith to us from Hajjaj.

Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Abi Hazim narrated to us: My father narrated to me, from 'Ubaydullah ibn Miqsam, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, who said: I saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, on the pulpit saying: "The Compeller, Mighty and Majestic, will take His heavens and His earths in His Hands..." then he mentioned the like of the hadith of Ya'qub.

Sa'id ibn Mansur narrated to us: Ya'qub—meaning Ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman—narrated to us: Abu Hazim narrated to me, from 'Ubaydullah ibn Miqsam, that he looked at 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar imitating the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, saying: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will take His heavens and His earths in His Hands and say: 'I am Allah'—and he clenches and uncurls his fingers—'I am the King,' until I looked at the pulpit shaking from its lowest part, to the extent that I was saying: 'Will it collapse with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him?'"

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from 'Umar ibn Hamzah, from Salim ibn 'Abdullah: 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar reported to me, saying: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will roll up the heavens on the Day of Resurrection, then take them in His Right Hand, then say: 'I am the King! Where are the tyrants? Where are the arrogant?' Then He will roll up the earths in His Left Hand, then say: 'I am the King! Where are the tyrants? Where are the arrogant?'"

Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me: Ibn Wahb reported to us: Yunus reported to me, from Ibn Shihab: Ibn al-Musayyab narrated to me that Abu Hurayrah used to say that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will seize the earth on the Day of Resurrection and roll up the sky in His Right Hand, then He will say: 'I am the King! Where are the kings of the earth?'"

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us; (and a different chain) Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and 'Ali ibn Khashram both narrated to us: 'Isa ibn Yunus reported to us; (and a different chain) 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, all of them from al-A'mash with this chain of narration, except that in all of their hadiths: "and the trees on a finger, and the soil on a finger," and not in the hadith of Jarir: "and the creation on a finger," but in his hadith: "and the mountains on a finger." And in the hadith of Jarir he added: "confirming him and marveling at what he said."

'Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us: My father narrated to us: Al-A'mash narrated to us, saying: I heard Ibrahim say: I heard 'Alqamah say: 'Abdullah said: A man from the People of the Book came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and said: "O Abu al-Qasim, indeed Allah holds the heavens upon one finger, the earths upon one finger, the trees and soil upon one finger, and all creation upon one finger, then He says: 'I am the King! I am the King!'" He said: I saw the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, laugh until his premolars showed, then he recited: {"And they did not appraise Allah with true appraisal"}.

'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim both narrated to us from Jarir, from Mansur with this chain of narration, saying: A Jewish rabbi came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, similar to the hadith of Fudayl, and he did not mention: "then He shakes them." And he said: I saw the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, laugh until his premolars showed, marveling at what he said and confirming him, then the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: {"And they did not appraise Allah with true appraisal"}, and he recited the verse.

Ahmad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Yunus narrated to us: Fudayl—meaning Ibn 'Iyad—narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from 'Abidah as-Salmani, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: A rabbi came to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and said: "O Muhammad," or "O Abu al-Qasim, indeed Allah the Exalted holds the heavens on the Day of Resurrection upon one finger, the earths upon one finger, the mountains and trees upon one finger, the water and soil upon one finger, and the rest of creation upon one finger; then He shakes them and says: 'I am the King! I am the King!'" The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, laughed in wonder at what the rabbi said and in confirmation of him, then he recited: {"And they have not appraised Allah with true appraisal, while the earth entirely will be within His grip on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded in His Right Hand. Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him"}.

Abu Bakr ibn Ishaq narrated to me: Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to us: Al-Mughirah—meaning al-Hizami—narrated to me, from Abu az-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said: "A large, fat man will come on the Day of Resurrection and will not weigh in the sight of Allah as much as the wing of a mosquito. Recite: {'So We will not assign to them any weight on the Day of Resurrection'}."

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Ya'qub—meaning Ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman al-Qari—narrated to us, from Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, the like of it, except that he said: "it darts toward this one once and toward this one once."

Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to me: My father narrated to us; (and a different chain) Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us, both saying: 'Ubaydullah narrated to us; (and a different chain) Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us—and the wording is his: 'Abd al-Wahhab—meaning ath-Thaqafi—reported to us: 'Ubaydullah narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said: "The likeness of the hypocrite is like that of a roaming ewe between two flocks, wandering toward this one at times and toward this one at other times."

'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-'Azim al-'Anbari narrated to me: Abu Muhammad an-Nadr ibn Muhammad ibn Musa al-Yamami narrated to us: 'Ikrimah narrated to us: Iyas narrated to us: My father narrated to me, saying: We visited with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, a man suffering from fever. He said: I placed my hand on him and said: "By Allah, I have never seen a man today with a hotter temperature than this." The Prophet of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Shall I not inform you of those hotter than him on the Day of Resurrection? Those two riders turning their backs"—referring to two men among his companions at that time.

Abu Kurayb Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to me: Hafs—meaning Ibn Ghiyath—narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, arrived from a journey, and when he was near Madinah, a violent wind blew that almost buried the rider. He asserted that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "This wind was sent due to the death of a hypocrite." When he arrived in Madinah, behold, a prominent hypocrite from among the hypocrites had died.

Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me: Abu an-Nadr narrated to us: Sulayman—namely Ibn al-Mughirah—narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: There was a man among us from Banu an-Najjar who had recited al-Baqarah and Al 'Imran, and he used to write for the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. He fled until he joined the People of the Book. He said: So they elevated him, saying: "This man used to write for Muhammad," and they were greatly pleased with him. Soon after, Allah broke his neck among them, so they dug for him and buried him. But the next morning, the earth had cast him up onto its surface. They returned, dug for him, and buried him, but the next morning, the earth had cast him up onto its surface. They returned again, dug for him, and buried him, but the next morning, the earth had cast him up onto its surface, so they left him cast aside.

Yahya ibn Habib al-Harithi narrated it to us: Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated to us: Qurrah narrated to us: Abu az-Zubayr narrated to us, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Whoever climbs the mountain path of al-Murar (or al-Marar)..." the like of the hadith of Mu'adh, except that he said: "and behold, it was a Bedouin who had come searching for a lost animal of his."

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh al-'Anbari narrated to us: My father narrated to us: Qurrah ibn Khalid narrated to us, from Abu az-Zubayr, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Whoever climbs the mountain pass, the pass of al-Murar, there will be remitted from him what was remitted from the Children of Israel." He said: The first to climb it were our horsemen, the horsemen of Banu al-Khazraj, and then the rest of the people arrived completely. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "All of you have been forgiven except the owner of the red camel." So we went to him and said: "Come, so that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, may ask forgiveness for you." He said: "By Allah, that I find my lost camel is more beloved to me than that your companion should ask forgiveness for me!" He said: And he was a man searching for a stray camel of his.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Abu Ahmad al-Kufi narrated to us: Al-Walid ibn Jumay' narrated to us: Abu at-Tufayl narrated to us, saying: There arose between a man from the people of al-'Aqabah and Hudhayfah some of what normally happens between people, so the man said: "I adjure you by Allah, how many were the people of al-'Aqabah?" He said: The people said to Hudhayfah: "Tell him since he has asked you." Hudhayfah said: We were told that they were fourteen; if you were among them, then the group was fifteen. And I testify by Allah that twelve of them are in open warfare against Allah and His Messenger in the worldly life and on the Day the witnesses stand forth; and he excused three, who said: "We did not hear the call of the caller of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, nor did we know what the group intended." The Prophet was in a stony tract and walked, saying: "The water is scarce, so let no one precede me to it." But he found a group who had preceded him, so he cursed them on that day.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn al-Muthanna's—they said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abu Nadrah, from Qays ibn 'Ubad, who said: We said to 'Ammar: "What do you think of this fighting of yours? Is it an opinion you have formed—for an opinion may be mistaken or correct—or a covenant that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, made with you?" He said: "The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, did not make any covenant with us that he did not make with all people generally." And he said: Indeed, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Indeed, in my nation..." Shu'bah said: and I believe he said: Hudhayfah narrated to me; and Ghundar said: I believe he said: "Among my nation there are twelve hypocrites who will not enter Paradise nor find its fragrance until the camel passes through the eye of the needle. Eight of them will be taken care of by the dubaylah: a spark of fire that appears between their shoulders until it erupts through their chests."
